problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $g(x,y)=\frac{y}{3x-y}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{y}).$
worked_solution:
A function $g(x,y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
g(tx,ty)={t}^{n}g(x,y).
$$

So first, we compute $g(tx,ty),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}g(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(tx,ty) & =\frac{ty}{3tx-ty}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{tx}{ty}) \\  & =\frac{ty}{t(3x-y)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{tx}{ty}) \\  & =\frac{t}{t}\cdot \frac{y}{3x-y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{y}) \\  & =\frac{y}{3x-y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{y}) \\  & =g(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${t}^{0}=1,$ the equality $g(tx,ty)=g(x,y)$ is equivalent to

$$
g(tx,ty)=1\cdot g(x,y)={t}^{0}g(x,y)
$$

and so the degree of the homogeneous function $g(x,y)$ is $0.$
